assets.title: Ambient Weather vs Flower Microclimate
assets.purpose: Show paired ambient and inflorescence temperature/RH measurements around a realistic dense cannabis flower and explain why sheltered flower conditions can differ from a nearby weather reading.
assets.diagnosticUse: Prevents a normal-looking ambient RH value from being used to dismiss persistent flower humidity risk.

assets.title: Rain & Dew — Flower Drying Timeline
assets.purpose: Track wetting start/end, visibly dry exterior, sheltered/interior persistence, wind, sun and humidity after a representative event.
assets.diagnosticUse: Shows why two storms with the same rainfall total can create different disease-weather pressure.

assets.title: Botrytis / Flower Rot — Early to Advanced Progression
assets.purpose: Show healthy flower, subtle early suspect tissue, localized internal browning/collapse, visible fungal development and advanced rot under consistent framing.
assets.diagnosticUse: Helps users recognize progression while emphasizing that visual appearance alone may not establish pathogen species.

assets.title: Flower Rot Look-Alikes
assets.purpose: Compare Botrytis-suspect rot with normal late-flower senescence, caterpillar/frass injury, physical breakage and rain-bruised tissue.
assets.diagnosticUse: Prevents brown flower tissue from being treated as a single-cause diagnosis and shows which evidence to inspect next.

assets.title: Flower Symptom Incidence & Severity Mapping
assets.purpose: Teach a defined flower sample, percent incidence, 0–4 severity classes and spatial mapping across canopy zones.
assets.diagnosticUse: Turns 'a few bad buds' into comparable evidence and reveals clustering in sheltered or repeatedly wet zones.

assets.title: Suspect Flower Triage & Sanitation Workflow
assets.purpose: Show photograph/map first, careful suspect-tissue handling, clean-tool/contact workflow, containment according to site rules and follow-up remeasurement.
assets.diagnosticUse: Reduces inspection-related spread risk and ensures response outcome is verified rather than assumed.
